retained_original_metadata.title: A nonzero-degree area-decreasing map, locally constant near infinity, from a complete noncompact even-dimensional spin manifold to the unit sphere forces strictly negative scalar curvature somewhere if the sphere bound holds on its differential support
retained_original_metadata.author: Weiping Zhang
retained_original_metadata.source_title: Nonnegative Scalar Curvature and Area Decreasing Maps
retained_original_metadata.difficulty_reason: The proof modifies a twisted Dirac operator by an odd endomorphism and a carefully selected cutoff, producing invertibility at infinity without requiring positive scalar curvature there. It divides the compact differential support into controlled norm regimes to obtain a nonnegative Bochner lower bound with a strictly positive mass region. The resulting zero-kernel index contradicts a nonzero relative degree index, strengthening the usual nonpositive-infimum conclusion to a strict inequality.
retained_original_metadata.source_version: Official SIGMA 16 (2020) article 033, DOI 10.3842/SIGMA.2020.033; journal PDF and native TeX acquired 2026-09-30, exact bytes pinned by SHA256

proof_review.method: Published author proof/core and local context fidelity screening
proof_review.note: Read all of the even-dimensional proof: graded spinor pullback, nowhere-zero-at-infinity potential, cutoff regions, deformed square/supercommutator calculation, relative index and three-region curvature estimates through the final contradiction. The relative index theorem, sphere-twisted Lichnerowicz curvature bound and characteristic-number evaluation are explicitly identified established background. The new deformation/cutoff positivity mechanism is supplied with the required compact support and small-epsilon bounds. Only Theorem2.1 is selected; odd-dimensional strict-hypothesis, circle stabilization and later weighted-curvature variants are not additional claims.

retained_original_metadata.statement_scope: Full Theorem2.1 in even dimension n>=2: M is a complete noncompact spin Riemannian n-manifold; smooth f:M->S^n(1) is area decreasing on two-forms, locally constant outside a compact set and of nonzero degree. Scalar curvature is at least n(n-1) on Supp(df). The conclusion is inf_M scalar curvature<0, not merely <=0. No strictly contracting map or positive-at-infinity scalar assumption is inserted.
